title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
abstract: In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point. Here, we deform the holographic dipole model so that its two coalescing scaling dimensions split into either two real ones or a complex-conjugate pair. We obtain the renormalized two-point functions in closed form. They change continuously from a linear combination of two power laws, through the logarithmic form of the LCFT at the exceptional point, to log-periodic oscillations. For any pair of scalar primary operators with real mixing under dilatations, the conformal Ward identities fix this form up to two normalization constants, which the holographic dictionary determines. In PT-symmetric theories with such a dilatation operator, real and complex-conjugate scaling dimensions correspond to the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases. In the BTZ black hole at finite temperature, the difference between the quasinormal frequencies associated with the two scaling dimensions changes from purely imaginary to purely real across the real-to-complex spectral transition. Correspondingly, the linear response changes from overdamped to underdamped, with critical damping at the exceptional point.
summary: This paper uses the AdS/CFT correspondence to study how correlation functions change when a quantum system undergoes a PT symmetry-breaking transition. By deforming a holographic model, the authors show that the two-point functions smoothly transition between power-law, logarithmic, and log-periodic behaviors. This provides a concrete holographic realization of spectral transitions seen in non-Hermitian quantum mechanics.
main_problem: The study investigates how holographic two-point functions behave across a quantum phase transition characterized by the breaking of Parity-Time (PT) symmetry.
main_result: The two-point functions continuously change functional form, transitioning from power laws (PT-unbroken) through a logarithmic form (exceptional point) to log-periodic oscillations (PT-broken).
method: The authors employ the AdS/CFT correspondence, calculating renormalized two-point functions in the bulk and deriving them from conformal Ward identities on the boundary.
model_or_system: The model is a deformation of the holographic dipole model in AdS spacetime, describing a system whose scaling dimensions transition between real and complex-conjugate pairs.
key_observables: Renormalized two-point functions $\langle O_a O_b angle$, and the real-time linear response (e.g., quasinormal frequencies).
important_parameters: The deformation parameter $\epsilon$, which controls the transition across the exceptional point ($\epsilon=0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed at leading semiclassical order, relying on the AdS/CFT correspondence and specific counterterms for renormalization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the splitting of scaling dimensions across $\epsilon$, the functional change of two-point functions across the exceptional point, and the transition of the real-time response from overdamped to underdamped.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the equations of motion, derives the two-point functions for different regimes ($\epsilon>0, \epsilon=0, \epsilon<0$), and confirms the continuity of the results using conformal Ward identities.
why_interesting: The connection between non-Hermitian physics (PT-symmetry breaking) and holographic dualities provides a powerful, geometric framework for understanding spectral transitions in quantum field theories.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Scaling dimensions ∆± as a function of ϵ. (a,b) The real (a) and imaginary (b) parts of ∆±, for d = 3 and m2 = −1. The two dimensions are real and different for ϵ > 0, coalesce at the exceptional point (EP) ϵ = 0, and form a complex-conjugate pair for ϵ < 0 (shaded). In PT- symmetric theories with the same structure, the two regimes are the PT-unbroken and PT-broken phases (section 5). See section 2 for details.

Figure 2. Two-point function ⟨O1(x1)O1(x2)⟩, multiplied by r2 ¯∆, as a function of ln r with r in units of the AdS radius, for d = 3 and m2 = −1. (a) Real scaling dimensions, ϵ = 0.1: linear combination of two power laws. The dashed curves are the contributions proportional to r−2∆+

Figure 3. Thermal retarded response ⟨O1O1⟩R at x = 0, multiplied by e2πTH ¯∆t, against time, in the BTZ black hole (d = 2) with m2 = −0.5. (a) ϵ = 0.1: overdamped, two decay rates. The dashed curves are the contributions that decay as e−2πTH∆±t at late times. (b) Exceptional point, ϵ = 0: critically damped, linear in t at late times. (c) ϵ = −0.2: underdamped, oscillation with frequency 2πTHκ. The dashed lines are its late-time envelope. Compare with the dependence on ln r in figure 2. See section 5.3 for details.
